scope: Single-Implementer post-acceptance correction requested by the owner after the 438b21d0 audit. Preserve the historical ACCEPTED record; fix delayed stale-reclaimer ABA in the existing MW10 repository and identical MW9 sibling, isolate the pre/post-acceptance control test fixtures, and restore the exact historical R2 verdict carriers. No MVP activation, registry/lease change, or historical evidence rewrite. This bounded repair proposal is not a new main-owned runtime activation or an independent verdict.

design_brief.problem_statement: R1 may observe stale owner A, then quarantine live successor B after another reclaimer removes A. A third writer can acquire while B is active. Post-acceptance Project Control also assumes absent acceptance in a live-main-derived fixture, and the canonical acceptance references two R2 verdict files present only in an unmerged carrier branch.
design_brief.current_behavior: 438b21d0 contains accepted P7 runtime and prior genuine 330-stage / 29-leaf passes, but its post-acceptance Project Control run 34173113080 fails test_valid_hold_routes_without_loading_obsolete_execution (expected 8, actual 0). The previous algorithm replay is a counterexample, not a full production repository test.
design_brief.desired_behavior: A reclaimer can act only on the observed token-specific owner marker; live successor markers remain nonempty and cannot be removed by rmdir. Native production-method regression proves the counterexample and the correction for MW9 and MW10. Both acceptance states are explicit isolated Git fixtures. Historical R2 records resolve from ordinary repository paths and remain attributed to their original subjects.
alternatives_considered: Repeat token checks after directory quarantine (still exposes a free canonical name)
Add sleeps/timeouts or rerun until pass (does not eliminate the race)
Native OS flock (requires unavailable portable engine API/GDExtension)
Token-addressed owner files and atomic empty-directory cleanup
design_brief.selected_design: Acquire publishes a prepopulated directory with a 256-bit random token-addressed owner file. Release atomically renames that specific file; stale reclaim removes only the exact observed filename. Directory removal is empty-only and never recursively deletes a current owner. UNKNOWN liveness remains fail-closed regardless of elapsed time. Old owner.json is read-only migration support under an explicitly quiescent all-writer upgrade.
design_brief.why_selected: Preserves the existing repository owner, directory acquisition primitive, CAS/checkpoint/pending-file protocol, release retry hook and bounded waits while removing the reusable-directory-name ABA window.
affected_owners: HARNESS test fixtures and evidence documentation
dependencies: Same-host private filesystem and shared PID namespace as the existing lock contract
All repository writers upgraded together; mixed old/new concurrent writers unsupported
non_goals: Rewrite an epoch or the existing acceptance

expected_risks: Full-regression exposure of another unrelated defect
validation_plan: Git blob verification of both originals and unchanged checkpoint/CAS methods

Candidate full native lock suite including UNKNOWN owner and reported-error-after-release with successor
Existing MW9 release retry and MW9/MW10 process recovery tests
Complete discovered world/core suite, no script exclusions
Full Harness regression and standard/directional PC0
Digest-bound clean HEAD/TREE logs and archive identity
Fresh independent Reviewer and Verifier on the final candidate before any merge proposal

Complete candidate evidence and independent verdicts
